eval.title: IBM Stock Analysis - 5.2% Dividend - Hybrid Cloud Growth, but...

call.headline_quote: i personally will not invest in ibm and really not even follow it because because it's ugly and i think i can find better

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: i have looked at the cash flows and we have free cash flows of around 11 12 billion conservatively 11

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: 20 chance on it going higher doubling on five percent steady growth over the next few years on on hybrid cloud

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: 60 change of it's staying in this range saved by the dividend

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: a 20 chance of a dividend cut and down to 60 on even slower growth losing that market share to amazon to all the clouds operators

what_is_priced_in.quote: if there would be no issues then this would be a 30 price earnings ratio 40 dividend yield of 1 company but it isn't

reasons.claim: IBM's revenue and net income have collapsed for nearly a decade, showing terrible underlying business performance.
reasons.quote: ibm's revenue growth went from 106 billion in 2012 to the current 75 billion they lost more than 25 of their revenue over the last eight years that's terrible

data_check.gap_note: he says 1.06e+11, as-of 7.7147e+10 (FY2019); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Long-term debt has ballooned versus free cash flow, leaving little room for buybacks, M&A, or flexibility, and it will take years to fix.
reasons.quote: 55 billion in debt which is huge compared to 12 billion in free cash flow that's four or five years of free cash flows

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: long-term debt

reasons.claim: CEO compensation soared massively even as the company and market cap collapsed, signaling management is not aligned with shareholders.
reasons.quote: the ceo romiti went from a compensation of 16 million in 2012 when she became ceo to 158 million in 2019 while the market capitalization simply disintegrated

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: ceo comp 2012, ceo comp 2019

reasons.claim: IBM prioritized protecting margins over growth-oriented acquisitions to please Wall Street, unlike Amazon, which cost them the last decade.
reasons.quote: ibm says how they could not do the deals they wanted to do because it might have been diluting their margins so they would not make an acquisition

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

reasons.claim: Despite the ugliness, IBM's entrenched infrastructure and sticky clients (e.g. credit card processing) make the dividend relatively safe.
reasons.quote: 90 of your credit card transactions go through ibm infrastructures etc so ibm is still ibm

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: credit card transaction share

external_facts_used: 30+ analyst reports reviewed for market sentiment
CEO's mid single digit growth guidance after separation
hybrid cloud $1 trillion market opportunity estimate
planned revenue split into $59 billion and $19 billion companies
historical buyback total of $200 billion over 30 years
comparison to Buffett's IBM buy in 2011 and sale

critic.notes: He personally passes ('will not invest... not even follow'), but calls it an interesting opportunity for dividend investors, 9% FCF yield, dividend safe, 'most probably the stock will do well' — fits fair_hold (not a bad addition even if he passes) rather than avoid.
